See It In Action

What PAR looks like

A live, sortable table of every report currently being measured or QC'd — filters, timers, and details all in one window, in light or dark mode.

PAR — Prod Active Reports · Light theme

Light theme — the Measure tab, filtered to Live reports across Manila, Cebu, and Bogota.

PAR — Prod Active Reports · Dark theme

Dark theme — the same view. Switch themes with one click and PAR remembers your choice.

Measure

✅

Features

Everything you need, at a glance

PAR is built to answer "what's going on right now?" instantly — no digging required.

⏱️

Live timers

Elapsed time and due-in countdowns update in real time, with overdue reports flashing so nothing slips by.

🔍

Instant search

Type to filter across any tab instantly. Your last search is remembered the next time you open PAR.

📌

One-click status filters

Click a status pill like "RTM" or "Due" to filter the table to just that group — click again to clear it.

🎓

Live / Training toggle

Show or hide training reports separately from live production work, so your view stays focused.

📍

Location filters

Narrow the view to Manila, Cebu, or Bogota — or see all three sites together.

🧩

Customizable columns

Show only the columns you care about. Your layout is saved automatically for next time.

🚩

Duplicate work alerts

If the same tech shows up on more than one in-progress report, PAR flags it so it can be caught early.

📋

Queue counts

Check live queue counts for drops, RTM, RFQC, and Hipster queues — and copy them to your clipboard in one click.

⬇️

Export to CSV

Export exactly what you see — your visible columns, your filtered rows — to a spreadsheet in one click.

🔄

Always fresh

The dashboard auto-reloads every few minutes to keep data current, and pauses automatically while you're viewing a report.

🌗

Light & dark mode

Switch themes with one click. PAR remembers your preference for next time.

🕒

Three-site clock

See the current time in Manila, the US, and Bogota at a glance, with day/night icons.

On the EVM Data tab, the Rollback menu lists every saved version of the report’s file, latest first. Pick one to see its counts, techs, QCs, and notes.

Double-click any report for the full story

No need to leave PAR to get context on a report — everything you need opens right there in a detail view.

  • Report images and wireframe tiles, viewable full-size
  • Address, product type, and key report info
  • EVM Data tab: roof, penetration, and wall counts, who worked on it and for how long, and the file notes, read from the report's latest rollback
  • Rollback menu: pick any saved rollback and PAR loads its EVM details and wireframes
  • Full history of the report's status changes
  • Rework details when a report's been sent back
  • One-click shortcuts to open the file location or map
Wireframe Preview

Preview the measurement without opening the file

See exactly what was measured — drawn on the photos and in 3D — right inside PAR.

New No need to open the file. PAR draws the wireframe for you, so you can check a measurement in seconds.
PAR — Wireframe preview

Ortho view — the measurement drawn directly on the top-down photo, with roof pitches labeled.

3D wireframeRotate, pan, and zoom the full model, with a count of facets by type.
North, East, West & South viewsThe same wireframe lined up on each angled photo, named by the wall it shows. Shown: North.
🖼️

Measurement on the photos

Flip through all six views with the arrows — Ortho (2D), Wireframes (3D), and the North, East, West, and South photos, each named by the wall it shows.

🧊

Interactive 3D model

Drag to rotate, right-drag to pan, scroll to zoom, and double-click to reset the view. Auto-rotate is one click away.

🎛️

Show only what you need

Toggle roofs, walls, pitch, holes, objects, and more, show roof and wall IDs, and adjust shading and transparency.

🗂️

Pick a rollback

Open the Rollback menu — on the EVM Data tab, in any photo preview, or in the 3D viewer — and pick any saved rollback. PAR loads that rollback’s EVM details and redraws the Ortho, 3D, and North, East, West, and South wireframes from it. The photos stay the same.

🏠

Hipster reports too

Hipster reports get a 3D wireframe as well, built from the Hipster job, alongside the photo views.

🔗

One setting, every view

Change a toggle in any preview and it applies to all of them, so you don't have to set it again on each photo.

🗂️ How the Rollback menu works. The latest rollback is selected by default. Choosing another one in any menu updates the others, and the EVM details and wireframes switch together. The menu is locked while a rollback is being drawn, and if one can’t be drawn PAR goes back to the one that was showing. Reports with only one rollback, and Hipster reports with no EVM file, have nothing to choose.
First Time Only

How to run PAR

You only need to do this once — after that, PAR lives on your desktop.

1
Copy and paste this into your File Explorer address bar:
📁 P:\1_Coordinators\PIA\PAR.lnk
💡 This is one time only. Running it will create a PAR shortcut on your Desktop — from then on, just double-click that shortcut to launch PAR.
Look for this on your Desktop This is the PAR shortcut icon — double-click it any time to launch the app.
2
A startup window appears — this is what it looks like:

Each step gets a green tick when it is done, and the log underneath shows what PAR is doing. The dashboard opens by itself at the end. You can click Hide to close the window; PAR keeps loading.

⏳ The first launch can take a few minutes. On first run PAR sets up Python 3 for your user account and installs the packages it needs (numpy, scipy, matplotlib). This happens one time only, so please keep PAR open until the dashboard appears. Later launches are much quicker.
Getting Started

Up and running in seconds

No accounts to create and nothing to install by hand — just open it and go.

1

Open PAR from your desktop

Double-click the PAR shortcut — it's kept up to date automatically.

2

Pick your tab

Choose Measure or QC depending on what you're working on.

3

Search, filter, and dig in

Use search, filters, and columns to find what matters, then double-click any report for full details.
